transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I'm just really struggling because I can’t stop fixating on how bad I look in every single picture, and it’s starting to seriously interfere with my work and social life. It's honestly getting to the point where I feel so overwhelmed and anxious all the time.

When you feel anxious, is it mainly because you believe there is something wrong with your appearance, or is it more that you fear being judged or embarrassed in social situations even aside from how you look?

It’s definitely because of how I look, not a general fear of being social, since I actually used to love planning events and being active in my community. The anxiety only happens because I can't stop fixating on how huge and crooked my nose looks and how uneven my skin is. I'm just terrified of people seeing me look like that, especially in photos.

Do you think your nose and skin really do look obviously defective to other people, or is part of you aware that you may be seeing them as worse than they actually are? How certain are you about that?

Even though my family and friends tell me I look fine and don't notice anything, it's really hard to believe them because the flaws on my nose and skin feel so real and obvious to me. I feel completely certain that I look terrible, which is why I end up spending hours zooming in on photos and picking myself apart.

Has there ever been any moment when you could consider that your nose and skin might not actually look as defective as they seem to you, or are you completely convinced that other people can clearly see these flaws? Do you ever think your mind might be exaggerating them at all?

It is incredibly hard to believe people like my mom or roommate when they tell me I look fine, because the flaws feel so obvious and huge to me. When I look in the mirror or at photos, my crooked nose and uneven skin completely consume me, and I'm convinced that's what everyone else is seeing too. That's why I keep asking for reassurance, even though their answers never actually make me feel any better.

Have you ever thought that your mind might be exaggerating these appearance flaws, even a little, or are you completely certain they are real and obvious to everyone? Has that level of certainty ever changed at all?
I'm not really sure, and I haven't really thought about whether my mind is exaggerating things. It's just that when I look at the photos, the flaws seem incredibly real and obvious to me.

When other people tell you your nose and skin look normal, can you ever consider they might be right, even briefly, or do you feel completely certain they are wrong? Have you ever changed your mind about this at all?

I'm not really sure, because it just feels so incredibly real to me when I look at myself. I haven't really thought about whether they could be right, I just can't shake the feeling that they are just saying that to be nice.

Outside of photos or mirrors, do you ever have moments when you can admit the problem might be less noticeable than it feels to you? Or are you certain all the time that other people can clearly see these flaws?

I am certain all the time that these flaws are obvious, and I find it incredibly hard to believe anyone who says otherwise. Even when my roommate or coworkers reassure me, I'm convinced they are just trying to be nice while my crooked nose and uneven skin remain glaringly visible to everyone. I just can't shake the feeling that it's always completely noticeable.

Has any doctor or dermatologist ever told you there is no significant problem with your nose or skin, and if so, were you able to accept that at all? Or did you still feel completely certain something was seriously wrong with how you look?

I haven't actually seen a doctor or a dermatologist about my nose or skin, so I'm not really sure how to answer that part. But even though other people keep telling me I look fine, I still feel completely certain that my nose is crooked and my skin is uneven.

Because of these concerns about your nose and skin, do you spend a lot of time doing things like checking mirrors, comparing yourself with other people, picking at your skin, or trying to hide the areas? About how many hours a day does this take?

Yes, I easily spend hours every day on these behaviors. I take dozens of selfies to check angles, constantly redo my makeup to hide my nose and skin, and change outfits three or four times before work. I also spend hours zooming in on photos to pick apart my flaws and constantly ask my mom or roommate for reassurance.

Do you believe your nose and skin problems are definitely real and visible to others, or is there any part of you that thinks these worries might be exaggerated by your mind? Have you ever sought cosmetic treatment or avoided it because others disagreed with you?

To me, the flaws on my nose and skin feel completely real and obvious, and I can't help but fixate on them even though everyone tells me they don't notice anything. I haven't actually sought out any professional cosmetic treatments, but I spend a massive amount of effort trying to camouflage these flaws myself using makeup, clothing, and camera angles.

The concern causes marked anxiety and interferes with work and social functioning. The focus is specifically on appearance rather than general social evaluation, supporting body dysmorphic disorder. Insight appears poor to absent/delusional intensity, but within ICD-10 this remains coded under hypochondriacal disorder/body dysmorphic disorder.
